title: A DMRG stall that regime labels 'converged' (Hubbard L=60 U=4): check whether chem-4e9 catches it

title: H-chain thermodynamic limit to n~40 with a systematic-inclusive error bar
description:
The committed headline e_inf = -0.539967 ± 0.000107 Ha/atom (n<=16) misses the published Simons/Motta DMRG STO-6G TDL value -0.540493 (PRX 7, 031059) by ~5x its own error bar (specs/BACKLOG.md:440-452). The ± is a fit stderr that tracks scatter, not the finite-size bias: e_inf drifts monotonically with n_max. The uncommitted 2026-07-04 run to n<=20 gives -0.540080 ± 0.000075, but its largest points are out of regime (stderr 0.83 mHa at n=20, 2.4 mHa at n=22; E/atom is non-monotone at n=22), and its bulk per-site estimate (-0.540818) disagrees with the 1/n fit by 0.74 mHa/atom. Note that SPEC_hchain_largen2.md:3-9 still says 'not yet executed'. That is stale: it was run, it cost ~21 h to n=20 on canonical orbitals, and it was killed at n=24.

WORK (after the localized-orbital bead shows the cost drop): uv run python benchmark_hchain_tdl.py --protocol ramp --localize --ns 8,10,12,16,20,24,28,32,40 --bond-dims 250,500,1000 --threads 4 --stack-mem-gb 6. The driver is resumable. Run the largest n last and stop cleanly if the time budget runs out; a clean n<=32 result beats a killed n<=40 one. Report e_inf from BOTH routes, the 1/n fit and bulk_per_site_energy, across several fit windows.

CLOUD SETUP: `uv sync --extra dmrg --extra test` (Linux x86_64; do NOT install the gpu extra; there is no CUDA). block2 segfaults when it shares a process with pyscf/qiskit-aer, so run each spec gate in its own process (`make gates`, or `scripts/run_gates.sh`; `GATE_JOBS=1` if one gets SIGKILLed). data/ is gitignored, so a fresh clone has none of the recorded CSVs: regenerate what you need, and put every number you report into a TRACKED file (the spec, or a vendored table the gate reads), never only into data/. Deliver the result as a branch + PR, not a push to main.

(3) The 1/n fit and bulk_per_site_energy agree to <0.1 mHa/atom. (4) e_inf is quoted with a systematic-inclusive bar (the spread across fit windows, not the fit stderr) and compared with -0.540493, stated as 'within' or 'outside' that bar with no hedging. (5) The per-n table is vendored into a tracked file and read by a spec gate; SPEC_hchain_largen2.md status is corrected, and BACKLOG.md:440 is resolved or updated. (6) If the result still disagrees with Motta, record that; don't tune the fit window to close the gap.

Headline e_inf = -0.540353 ± 0.000192 Ha/atom (8-fit envelope + max stderr). Motta -0.540493 is INSIDE (0.73 bar). All four a+b/n+c/n^2 fits give -0.540492..-0.540496. LOO 0.037 mHa PASS; bulk vs a+b/n fit 0.232 mHa FAIL (reported: the 1/n form is wrong at n<=40). n=48/56 were OOM-killed at 15 GiB. The old headline -0.539967 ± 0.000107 is superseded. title: H-chain DMRG: localized site orbitals, validated against FCI, with a cost probe at n=20
description:
Every H-chain DMRG run so far used canonical, delocalized RHF orbitals: benchmark_hchain_tdl.py integrals() passes mf.mo_coeff straight through, and dmrg_reference.py calls initialize_system(orb_sym=None) with no localization or reordering. For a 1D chain, delocalized orbitals make entanglement grow with n. That plausibly explains why the large-n run cost ~21 h for n<=20 on the laptop (logs/hchain_pipeline.log: n=8..20 took 2026-07-04 04:50 to 07-05 01:53; the n=22/24 stage was killed after ~19.5 h), and why SPEC_hchain_largen recorded 'D needed grows with n'. The literature H-chain benchmarks (Hachmann/Chan; Motta et al. PRX 7, 031059) use localized orbitals. This is an INFERENCE from the code, not yet measured; this bead measures it.

WORK: add a --localize option to integrals() (Löwdin/meta-Löwdin orthogonalized site orbitals over the FULL basis, in chain order). A unitary rotation of the full space leaves the FCI energy unchanged exactly, and DMRG energies converge to the same limit. Then run the cost probe: n=20, D=400, canonical vs localized, same sweeps, recording the discarded weight, the energy and the wall time for each.

CLOUD SETUP: `uv sync --extra dmrg --extra test` (Linux x86_64; do NOT install the gpu extra; there is no CUDA). block2 segfaults when it shares a process with pyscf/qiskit-aer, so run each spec gate in its own process (`make gates`, or `scripts/run_gates.sh`; `GATE_JOBS=1` if one gets SIGKILLed). data/ is gitignored, so a fresh clone has none of the recorded CSVs: regenerate what you need, and put every number you report into a TRACKED file (the spec, or a vendored table the gate reads), never only into data/. Deliver the result as a branch + PR, not a push to main.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Localized-orbital FCI matches canonical FCI at n=8,10,12 to <1e-8 Ha, added as a spec gate next to G1 in tests/test_hchain_tdl_spec.py. (2) At n=10 and 12, localized DMRG matches FCI to <1e-6 Ha. (3) Recorded for the n=20, D=400 probe, both bases: E, discarded weight, wall time and threads. (4) A one-line verdict in SPEC_hchain_largen2.md: does localization cut the D needed at fixed accuracy, and by how much? If it does NOT, say so plainly; the downstream beads then need re-scoping, not a bigger machine.
close_reason: Done via PR #39 (merged into certkit-integration at 801b445). Löwdin site orbitals behind --localize; FCI invariant to <1e-10 at n=8,10,12; localized G1 converged regime; D=1000 n=12 within 2.2e-11 of FCI. n=20 probe (Xeon, 4 threads): canonical D=400 is 6.4e-3 Ha above the best energy after 572 s without converging; localized D=100 reaches 5.7e-8 in 38 s. D cut >=8x, time >=29x (both lower bounds). Independently reproduced 2026-09-24 in a Linux arm64 container: the 3 G1 gates pass and localized n=20 D=100 gives E=-10.825878811 (identical). Also fixed a latent bug: fci_energy silently returned unconverged Davidson energies (follow-up chem-3f8). macOS DMRG is currently broken by a duplicate libomp (chem-dfe), unrelated to this change.

title: compile_from_gcs labels geometries by nearest-CASCI match, destroying the reference check
description: compile_from_gcs.py recovers which geometry produced each GCS result by computing local CASCI energies for every candidate coordinate and taking the argmin of |E_solver - E_CASCI| (accepting under 1e-4 Ha), with a comment asserting the closest match is 'mathematically guaranteed to be correct'. It is not: it is circular. The coordinate label is derived FROM the reference, so any later comparison of that dataset against CASCI is guaranteed to agree to <1e-4 by construction and can no longer falsify anything. identify_family_by_energy() compounds this with hardcoded energy windows. This violates the repo's falsifiable-honesty rule that every result carries a reference that could kill it. Fix: have the worker persist the request geometry into the result blob (or key blobs by a content hash of the request) so provenance is recorded, not inferred.
acceptance_criteria: result JSON carries the originating molecule/basis/active_space; compile path reads provenance rather than matching energies; any CASCI comparison is then an independent check
close_reason: Provenance now stated by the producer: EnergyRequest takes optional bounded metadata, worker stamps molecule/basis/active_space/mode/krylov_dim/job_id/metadata into every result blob, compile_from_gcs reads those labels and skips (never guesses) provenance-less blobs. Circular identify_family_by_energy + CASCI-argmin matching deleted along with the duplicated geometry tables. --verify makes the CASCI comparison a real independent check on bracket containment. 14 tests in tests/test_certchem_provenance.py. Commit 51d92d9.

title: run_grand_sweep: ethylene torsion submits 7 identical geometries
description: generate_experiments()['ethylene_torsion'] computes rad = deg*pi/180 and never uses it; y_r/z_r are hardcoded constants (y*0.86, z*0.50), so all 7 torsion angles 0-90deg produce a byte-identical molecule string. Verified: 7 points -> 1 distinct geometry. The 'diradical transition state at 90 degrees' this family claims to probe is never computed. compile_from_gcs.py:ethylene_geom(deg) has the same defect and ignores its deg argument, so the recovery path would happily label 7 copies of one energy as a torsion curve. Fix: rotate the second CH2 plane by rad about the C-C axis.
acceptance_criteria: 7 torsion points yield 7 distinct geometries; energy at 90deg differs measurably from 0deg; a test asserts len(set(geoms))==7
close_reason: ethylene_geometry(deg) now rotates the C2 methylene about the C-C axis; 7 angles -> 7 distinct geometries, dihedral matches request, bond lengths/angles invariant. CASCI(2,2)/sto-3g barrier +86.0 kcal/mol, monotonic. compile_from_gcs imports the single generator. Gate in tests/test_ethylene_torsion.py, verified failing pre-fix. Commit 574b8e8.

title: Committed NbN SCF reference (data/nbn_scf.chk, S=3 sector) sits at a threading-nondeterministic, marginally-unstable UHF solution
description: chem-owr diagnosed why nbn_low_spin.py scan doesn't reproduce the committed chk energy at d=3.7255 A: it is NOT a geometry/basis/ECP/MIC bug in the scan reconstruction (all verified identical to <2e-5 A and identical basis/ECP assignment). The root cause is that the committed high-spin (10,4)/S=3 UHF solution sits essentially exactly at a pyscf internal-stability boundary (a near-zero Hessian eigenvalue in benchmark_nbn._tight_scf's stability-following loop). Whether pyscf's Davidson-based stability() call reports 'stable' (keeping the higher-energy committed solution) or 'unstable' (following it down 0.548 mHa in SCF / 4.84 mHa in downstream CAS(14,14) FCI(10,4)) depends on default multi-threaded BLAS floating-point non-associativity: with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, two independent fresh SCF runs on the real geometry (specs/nbn_mp-2634.cif) deterministically and reproducibly (bit-identical, e_tot=-110.02813374576796 both times) find the instability and land on the LOWER, more-stable solution; with default multi-threading, 3 of 4 trials found the same lower solution but 1 of 4 reproduced the committed higher (metastable) energy (-110.02758538272639, matching specs/nbn_scf_reference.chk's -110.0275853827266 to 9 decimals). This means the currently-vendored NbN SCF reference (specs/nbn_scf_reference.chk / data/nbn_scf.chk), and every number built on it across nbn_dmrg_reference.py, SPEC_nbn_dmrg_reference.md (G1-G3b), and SPEC_nbn_low_spin.md (Tables 1-2, the S1-S3 gap, the G4/G5 gates), is anchored to a UHF solution that the SAME current code, run deterministically (single-threaded), reproducibly finds is NOT the lowest/most-stable one available in the (10,4) sector. Needs: (1) decide whether to re-vendor a chk from the deterministic single-threaded lower-energy solution, or keep the current one with an explicit caveat that it is metastable; (2) if re-vendored, every downstream gate/table anchored to the old chk's energy needs re-deriving, which is substantial (touches chem-bbi's G3/G3b, chem-g1i's Tables 1-3/G4/G5 -- both already-closed beads). Reproducing commands and full trial-by-trial numbers are in sandbox-handoffs/chem-owr.md and specs/SPEC_nbn_low_spin.md section 0/7/8 (2026-09-27 update).
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) a decision + re-vendored chk + updated downstream gates/tables/specs all green, with the re-derivation documented and cross-checked; or (b) an explicit, spec-recorded decision to keep the current metastable chk as the reference with a caveat on every table/gate that depends on it, plus a determinism-forcing fix (e.g. pin OMP_NUM_THREADS or a tighter stability check) so future regenerations are reproducible rather than a coin flip.
notes: Resolved via acceptance-criteria path (b). Decision recorded in specs/SPEC_nbn_low_spin.md §0 (+ G4/G5 caveats) and specs/SPEC_nbn_dmrg_reference.md §8 R4 (covers G1-G3b): keep the vendored metastable chk as reference, caveat every dependent gate/table. Determinism fix: benchmark_nbn._tight_scf now pins pyscf.lib.num_threads(1) for the SCF+Newton+stability loop, restored after. New gate tests/test_nbn_scf_determinism_spec.py (G1 cross-thread, G2 repeat-call) — RED confirmed before fix, GREEN after (2 passed, 22.86s). Re-ran test_nbn_dmrg_reference_spec.py (4 passed, 341s) and test_nbn_low_spin_spec.py (2 passed, 484s) each in own process to confirm no regression (neither imports benchmark_nbn, so unaffected by design). ruff clean on touched files. Full re-derivation on the alternate minimum declined (shared orbitals across all sectors make it a ~50-70min job, not a one-number fix) and filed as chem-czw. Full evidence/commands in sandbox-handoffs/chem-y6w.md. Tree left dirty per git policy — no commit/push made.
close_reason: Decision (b): kept vendored metastable chk as reference with explicit caveats on every dependent gate (SPEC_nbn_low_spin.md G4/G5, SPEC_nbn_dmrg_reference.md G1-G3b); fixed regeneration-path determinism via pyscf.lib.num_threads(1) pin in benchmark_nbn._tight_scf (SPEC_nbn_scf_determinism.md, G1/G2 green, RED confirmed pre-fix, re-verified green this session: 2 passed in 32.86s). Full re-derivation on the alternate minimum declined as out of scope, filed as chem-czw.

title: tests/test_lambda_ladder_honest_caveat_spec.py::test_G3 and test_shift_both_sides_spec.py::test_G5[H2] flaky: RHF/CASCI orbital gauge nondeterminism for degenerate systems
description:
Discovered while verifying chem-3f8's fix (unrelated to it -- reproduces identically on the original unmodified lambda_ladder.py/shift_both_sides.py via git stash, confirmed the fix did not cause it). Two spec gates are flaky across repeated 'uv run pytest' invocations in fresh processes, same inputs, same code:

1. tests/test_lambda_ladder_honest_caveat_spec.py::test_G3_df_rank_truncation_accuracy_is_not_monotonic (N2 CAS(4,3), sto-3g) -- asserts the DF rank-truncation FCI-error sweep is NOT monotonically decreasing (the spec's documented finding). Failed 2/5 runs; the per-rank error sequence itself differs numerically between process runs (e.g. one run: [77.03, 74.98, 6.59, 49.41, 50.15, 0.0] mHa: clearly non-monotonic and passes; another: [127.13, 99.63, 46.39, 42.26, 11.65, 5.7e-11]: monotonically decreasing and fails) even though double_factorize()'s g eigenvalues are close but not exactly degenerate (0.0846, 0.0763, 0.0691, 0.0561, 0.0451 -- see df_factorization.double_factorize output for this system).

2. tests/test_shift_both_sides_spec.py::test_G5_identity_term_inflates_the_gain[H2] -- 'assert inflated > honest' flips sign between runs (e.g. one run: inflated=2.563, honest=3.071 -- fails; the intent is inflated>honest).

Root cause not yet isolated but the leading suspect is RHF converging to an arbitrary rotation within a near-degenerate orbital subspace (N2's pi pair is exactly degenerate by symmetry; H2's minimal-basis case may have a similar near-tie) that varies run-to-run, likely from BLAS/LAPACK thread-count nondeterminism in eigh/SCF diagonalization -- NOT from double_factorize's own eigh call in isolation (repeated eigh calls on the SAME eri within one process are deterministic; the eri itself differs across fresh-process runs). Needs isolating whether it's mf.kernel()'s SCF orbitals, cas.kernel()'s CASCI step, or double_factorize's eigh that is the nondeterministic step, then either pinning BLAS threads (OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 / OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1) for reproducibility, or fixing the gauge (e.g. canonicalize degenerate-subspace orbitals) before these specs' assertions, or loosening/re-deriving the acceptance thresholds if the finding is gauge-dependent rather than a fixed fact about these systems.
acceptance_criteria: Both tests pass deterministically across >=10 repeated fresh-process pytest runs (or the spec is revised to state the gauge-dependence honestly, per specs/README.md's 'if a gate proves unsatisfiable, revise the spec and record why').
notes: LOCAL macOS RE-VERIFICATION 2026-09-27: acceptance NOT met. test_G5[H2] fails 7/7 fresh runs deterministically (inflated=4.701 vs honest=3.071; sandbox Linux got inflated=2.56). ROOT CAUSE (neither the BLAS-gauge story nor the 'deterministic counter-example' story): for even norb (H2 norb=2, N2(6,6) norb=6) lambda_DF is EXACTLY flat in b2 around the SCDF optimum (nuclear norm of h1+b2*I constant while b2 sits between the middle eigenvalues), so df_factorization.symmetry_shift's Nelder-Mead b2 is arbitrary/platform-dependent. The identity-inclusive lambda_meas varies linearly along that flat line (H2: 1.11-1.44 for b2 +/-0.1, lambda_DF fixed at 0.970698); N2's honest lambda_meas also moves at b2-0.1. H2O(4,3) (odd norb) has a unique optimum. So H2/N2 inclusive gains (and the N2 'inflated>12' headline) are optimizer-endpoint artifacts. The original committed '53.9%/4.70x' H2 row was NOT wrong -- it is exactly what macOS computes; the chem-1yr revision to 2.56x is equally arbitrary. Needs: canonical b2 tie-break on the flat interval, or restate G5 as b2-gauge-dependent for even norb.
close_reason: Local macOS re-verification found the real G5[H2] cause: lambda_DF is exactly flat in b2 for even norb, so Nelder-Mead's b2 was arbitrary per platform and moved only the identity-inclusive gain (macOS 4.70x, Linux 2.56x). The H2 'exception' is retracted. symmetry_shift now sets b2 analytically at the flat interval's midpoint (lambda_DF unchanged, H2O identical). G5 is back to 'every molecule' (5.33/4.24/14.32x inclusive vs 3.07/2.73/5.67x honest). Both gate files pass 10/10 fresh-process runs; scdf_lambda/precision_cost gates green. SPEC_shift_both_sides.md R3-R4.

title: SPEC_nbn_low_spin.md tables and G5 threshold need correction: reconstruction used wrong bond length
description:
chem-bbi (NbN reference reproducibility) found that chem-dc7's d=2.25A NbN reconstruction (specs/SPEC_nbn_low_spin.md) actually built a molecule with Nb-N separation 3.7255 A, not 2.25 A: benchmark_nbn.py's ground_state_mf builds atom_str from ASE's raw unwrapped atom.position values instead of the minimum-image-reduced distance (atoms.get_distance(i,j,mic=True) gives 2.2464 A, matching MP; the unwrapped atoms.get_distance(i,j) gives 3.7255 A). So every number in SPEC_nbn_low_spin.md Tables 1-3 (the 15.1 mHa S1-S3 gap, E0=-110.0712455 Ha, the nine-distance scan) describes a different, longer-bond molecule than the one this repo actually committed.

chem-bbi vendored the real, original data/nbn_scf.chk and its CIF (specs/nbn_scf_reference.chk, specs/nbn_mp-2634.cif) and reproduced the historically-committed E(10,4)=-110.046028 exactly from them. On this REAL geometry: exact FCI (Ms=0 sector, 1.18e7 dets) finds S=1 is the CAS ground at E=-110.04756504307636 Ha, only 1.538 mHa below the committed S=3 sector (E=-110.04602823118735 Ha, DMRG A'), not 15.1 mHa. S=0 (7,7) is +5.065 mHa above S=3. S=2 (9,5) has not been remeasured on the real geometry.

tests/test_nbn_low_spin_spec.py::test_G5_committed_sector_is_not_the_cas_ground asserts e_s1 < e_s3 - 5e-3 (a 5 mHa margin), calibrated against the wrong-bond-length reconstruction's 15.1 mHa gap. Against the real geometry (now the default resolved by load_nbn_cas's chk path after chem-bbi wired ensure_reference_data() into it) the real gap is only 1.538 mHa, so this assertion is expected to fail -- see the pytest run started at 2026-09-26T15:12 (log /tmp/test_low_spin2.log on this container) for the actual verdict.

Qualitative conclusion (S=1 is the true ground, S=3/committed is not) still holds on the real geometry -- only the gap's magnitude and Tables 1-3's absolute numbers need correcting.
acceptance_criteria: SPEC_nbn_low_spin.md Tables 1-3 either recomputed on the real, vendored geometry (specs/nbn_scf_reference.chk) or clearly re-labeled as describing a different (wrong-bond-length) molecule with no claim of applying to the committed one. test_nbn_low_spin_spec.py's G5 threshold recalibrated to the real S1-S3 gap (measured 1.538 mHa) or otherwise made consistent with the real geometry, with provenance. Full nbn low-spin gate suite green from a fresh clone.
notes: Confirmed 2026-09-26: chem-bbi's own gate (tests/test_nbn_dmrg_reference_spec.py, G1/G2/G3/G3b) is unaffected by the real geometry and passes -- 'uv run pytest -q tests/test_nbn_dmrg_reference_spec.py' -> '4 passed in 411.96s (0:06:51)'. This bead is scoped to the separate tests/test_nbn_low_spin_spec.py / SPEC_nbn_low_spin.md gates only, which fail as detailed in the prior note.
close_reason: SPEC_nbn_low_spin.md Tables 1-3 corrected to the real vendored geometry, G5 recalibrated to the measured 1.538 mHa gap, G4 replaced with the honest cheap-D-inconclusive/headline-D-soft finding. Gate suite 2/2 green. Handoff: sandbox-handoffs/chem-g1i.md. Out-of-scope finding filed as chem-owr.

title: Be2: basis-consistent active space, so TZ/QZ/5Z wells are comparable
description: chem-mom (PR #43): CAS(4,8) on canonical HF virtuals is a different active space in each basis. At R=2.5 Å the outermost active orbital's rms spread grows 7.1 -> 8.3 -> 9.4 bohr and its energy falls +0.150 -> +0.074 Ha, so the single-basis wells oscillate (997 -> 698 -> 1313 cm^-1) and no two-point CBS is meaningful. Choose an active space that is stable across bases (e.g. valence natural orbitals or AVAS-selected 2s2p), then rerun TZ/QZ/5Z and redo the method-vs-basis attribution with a pre-registered criterion.
acceptance_criteria: Active-space character documented per basis (spread, energy); single-basis De monotone or explained; CBS attribution re-tested against a pre-registered threshold.
close_reason: Done: AVAS(minao=ano)-selected CAS(4,8) makes the active space basis-consistent (spread agrees <0.01 bohr TZ vs 5Z, gated G1-G2), retested chem-mom's pre-registered CBS bar (G3): still NOT CONFIRMED but shift shrinks 1224->530 cm^-1; single-basis wells non-monotone but explained (TZ is the outlier, G4). See specs/SPEC_be2_avas_cbs.md and sandbox-handoffs/chem-xqh.md.

title: Certified two-sided H-chain bracket: VSDP-rigorous PQG+T2 lower bound + DMRG upper, n=12-16
description: Discovery shortlist #2 (portfolio notes/discovery-shortlist.md), verdict PARTIAL. Chaykin, Jansson, Keil et al. (JCTC 2020) made 2-RDM SDP lower bounds floating-point rigorous (VSDP) for small molecules. Rubin, Low, DePrince (arXiv 2602.05069) did SOS/v2RDM on hydrogen rings of 10-30 atoms without rigorous verification or accuracy against a reference. What would be new: a verified [lower, upper] bracket for open H_n beyond FCI size and its per-atom width vs n. It is an application of VSDP at scale, not a new method. The SDP solver is an untrusted producer; certkit or an interval check verifies the dual. Pre-registered kill: bracket width > 1 mHa/atom at n=12. Scale is limited by T2 SDP size on a 4-core, 15 GB VM, so realistically n=12-16. Depends on localized-orbital DMRG (chem-rhw, done) for the upper bound.
acceptance_criteria: At n=10 the certified lower bound is below FCI and the bracket contains FCI (sanity). At n=12,14,16 the rigorous lower bound and DMRG upper bound are reported with the certification method documented; width per atom vs n is tabulated; the kill test is evaluated and stated.

title: Implement SPEC_interval_dominance_screening: prune candidate libraries by certified bracket dominance
description:
Implement specs/SPEC_interval_dominance_screening.md (Proposed v1.0): use certified energy brackets at cheap Krylov dimension to prove a candidate cannot be the global minimum (L_j > U_best) and prune it before paying for full convergence.

Deliverables: screening_loop.py, tests/test_screening_loop_spec.py (G1-G4), data/screening_loop_performance.csv, spec revised to v2.0, BACKLOG entry.

REVIEW FLAGS (resolve or falsify, do not tune around):
1. LIKELY KILL - bracket looseness at cheap M. Pruning needs L_j(M) > U_best. SPEC_excited_state_certification just measured certified bracket widths of 88.3 mHa (LiH) and 981 mHa (H4) at low M, and temple_bounds lower bounds are looser still at M=2. If the M=2 bracket is hundreds of mHa wide, NOTHING prunes and the 75-80 percent saving is unreachable. Measure the actual bracket width vs the actual candidate spread FIRST, before building the loop - that single number decides whether this spec lives.
2. LIBRARY DEPENDENCE. The specced library is a geometry sweep of ONE molecule, whose candidates sit within mHa of each other near the minimum - the worst case for interval dominance. Savings are a property of the library's energy spread relative to bracket width, not of the method. Any percentage must be quoted with the library that produced it, and the spread/width ratio is the real gated quantity.
3. G3 'strictly non-increasing staircase' is VACUOUS - an active pool can only shrink by construction. Replace with a gate on how EARLY pruning happens (pool size at each M), which is what the economic claim rests on.
4. No QPU is involved. 'Saving QPU runtime' is simulated circuit/shot accounting; the cost model must be stated and its assumptions gated.
5. G1 zero-false-negatives is the soundness gate and matters most - a prune that drops the true winner invalidates everything. Test it against brute force on a library where brackets nearly overlap.
acceptance_criteria: make gates-screening_loop green; G1 soundness (no false prune of the true winner) proven against brute force; the achievable saving reported with the library spread/bracket-width ratio that produced it, or the spec honestly killed if cheap-M brackets cannot dominate; spec at v2.0 with v1.0 preserved; ruff clean; nothing committed without approval
close_reason: Closed

title: Implement SPEC_trotter_floor_restorer: pre-diagonalization Richardson on Trotter signals
description:
Implement specs/SPEC_trotter_floor_restorer.md (Proposed v1.0): extrapolate the complex Trotter survival-amplitude signal BEFORE diagonalization, so the variational-floor leak is plugged while Ritz vectors and variances survive for Lehmann certification (excited_bounds.py).

Deliverables: trotter_restorer.py, tests/test_trotter_restorer_spec.py (G1-G4), data/trotter_restorer_bench.csv, spec revised to v2.0 recording what held and what was falsified, BACKLOG entry.

REVIEW FLAGS (resolve or falsify, do not tune around):
1. TIME-ALIGNMENT BUG in spec 3.2. s_k(dt) sits at physical time k*dt, s_k(2dt) at 2k*dt. Richardson across the same index k compares DIFFERENT times, so the O(dt^2) term does not cancel. Correct pairing is likely s_2k(dt) vs s_k(2dt). Check before implementing; if the spec formula is wrong, that is the first finding.
2. G2 demands the restored energy sit ABOVE E_FCI. Richardson error is two-sided and ODMD/Krylov on an extrapolated signal is NOT variational (SPEC_odmd G2 already gates that). 'E >= E_FCI' is probably not a guarantee, only an observation at particular dt. Gate what is true.
3. G4 says 2x narrower than 'any attempt' to bound scalar_extrap - unfalsifiable as written. Needs one concrete named scalar-extrap bound to compare against.
4. G3 '100% sound across all step-sizes' - check whether soundness survives large dt where the Trotter sector itself shifts.

title: nbn_low_spin.py scan pipeline does not reproduce committed chk energy at matching bond length
description:
While correcting SPEC_nbn_low_spin.md (chem-g1i), re-ran nbn_low_spin.py scan at d=3.7255 A -- the
real Nb-N separation the committed data/nbn_scf.chk actually encodes (per chem-bbi's fix in
SPEC_nbn_dmrg_reference.md). Expected the scan pipeline's fresh SCF-from-synthetic-CIF reconstruction
to reproduce the committed chk's energy at this matching distance. It does not:

  E(10,4) scan  = -110.041189 Ha (exact FCI, synthetic single-cell CIF reconstruction)
  E(10,4) chk   = -110.046028 Ha (exact FCI, real vendored data/nbn_scf.chk)
  discrepancy   = 4.84 mHa

Ruled out: the scan pipeline's own MIC/unwrapping bug that caused the ORIGINAL wrong-bond-length
mislabeling (benchmark_nbn.ground_state_mf building atom_str from ASE's raw, unwrapped
atom.position). A direct check with nbn_low_spin.write_cif shows its own no-MIC and MIC distances
agree to machine precision at every d tried, including 3.7255 A -- so this is a different,
undiagnosed mismatch between the two code paths (candidates not yet ruled out: basis-set/ECP
assignment differences, SCF spin-scan differences, or a genuine remaining geometry difference e.g.
real mp-2634.cif lattice constants (a=2.97204749, c=2.89967487) vs write_cif()'s defaults).

Filed out of scope for chem-g1i, which only needed the already-established real-chk numbers
(Table 1), not the scan pipeline. Table 3 of SPEC_nbn_low_spin.md now carries an explicit caveat
that the scan pipeline's absolute energies should not be equated with the real-chk numbers.
notes: Diagnosed. NOT a geometry/basis/ECP/MIC bug in nbn_low_spin.py's scan reconstruction (verified: real vendored CIF gives Nb-N no-mic distance 3.7255149 A vs scan's target 3.7255000 A, basis/ECP assignment identical by construction). Root cause: the committed (10,4)/S=3 UHF solution in specs/nbn_scf_reference.chk sits essentially exactly at a pyscf internal-stability boundary. benchmark_nbn._tight_scf's Newton/SOSCF stability-following loop lands on one of (at least) two genuinely locally-stable UHF minima 0.548 mHa apart in SCF energy (4.84 mHa apart after CASCI(14,14)/FCI(10,4)) depending on multi-threaded BLAS floating-point non-associativity in pyscf's Davidson stability check -- NOT on any geometry difference. Reproduced: fresh SCF on the real CIF (specs/nbn_mp-2634.cif, no chk restore), default 8 threads, 4 trials -> 3 land on the lower solution, 1 reproduces the committed higher energy to 9 decimals. Same command with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 -> 2/2 trials bit-identically find the lower solution. Both solutions independently verified locally stable via explicit mf.newton().stability() checks. Updated specs/SPEC_nbn_low_spin.md sections 0, 7, 8 and the Table 3 caption with full diagnosis and reproducing commands. Filed chem-y6w (P2) for the follow-on question this raises: should the vendored chk (and everything built on it: chem-bbi's G3/G3b, chem-g1i's Tables 1-2/G4/G5) be re-anchored to the deterministic lower-energy solution? That is out of scope for chem-owr, which only asked why the scan pipeline disagreed with the chk -- now answered. No production code changed (only specs/SPEC_nbn_low_spin.md); no test files touched; ruff clean. Full writeup: sandbox-handoffs/chem-owr.md
close_reason: Diagnosed: not a code bug in nbn_low_spin.py's scan/geometry reconstruction (all three candidates the bead listed -- basis/ECP, spin-scan, geometry -- ruled out with direct evidence). Root cause is SCF-solution multiplicity (two genuinely locally-stable UHF minima 0.548 mHa apart in the committed (10,4)/S=3 sector) combined with BLAS-threading non-determinism in benchmark_nbn._tight_scf's pyscf stability-following loop, reproduced across 6 independent trials (4 default-thread, 2 single-thread deterministic). Full writeup in sandbox-handoffs/chem-owr.md; spec updated (specs/SPEC_nbn_low_spin.md sections 0/7/8 + Table 3). Consequence for the committed chk's own status filed as chem-y6w (P2), out of scope here.
